---
title: "google_analytics.meta_page_traffic"
description: "Daily readership of Signal Check, the dashboards, and the Cookbook, by page and session source."
---

Daily traffic for the meta-analytics GA4 property, which measures who reads
Signal Check, the published dashboards, and this Metrics Cookbook.

Each row represents one day of traffic to a single page, from sessions that
started from one source, medium, and campaign.

`Keywords`: Google Analytics, GA4, meta-analytics, Signal Check, dashboards, Metrics Cookbook, readership, page views, session source, utm_source

## Provenance

Pulled daily from the GA4 Data API (`runReport`) for the meta-analytics
property, by the same Lambda and pipeline as
[`page_traffic`](page_traffic.qmd). The Glue ETL job adds two derived
columns, `pagepath_redacted` and `page_kind`. They exist only in this table
and [`meta_page_events`](meta_page_events.qmd).

The property has two web streams. The Signal Check stream covers the Signal
Check editions and the published dashboards, which carry the same tag. The
Metrics Cookbook stream covers this site, including its PR previews.

Data starts on 2026-07-23.

* **Updated**: Daily, at 07:00 ET
* **Retention**: 7 years
* **Steward**: EDCP Data and Research Team
* **Contact**: [Colin Douglas](mailto:colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca)
* **Location**: `s3://<transformed-bucket>/google_analytics/meta_page_traffic/`

## Fields

One row per `date` per `streamid` per `pagepath` per `pagetitle` per
`sessionsource`, `sessionmedium`, and `sessioncampaignname`.

| Field Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| date | string | The reporting day, as a partition key (for example, "2026-09-22") |
| streamid | string | Numeric ID of the GA4 data stream that reported the page. Stable if a stream is renamed |
| streamname | string | Display name of the GA4 data stream, "Signal Check" or "Metrics Cookbook" |
| pagepath | string | The page's URL path as GA4 reports it. Signal Check paths include a private token. Do not use (see Notes) |
| pagetitle | string | The page's `<title>` at the time of the visit. Signal Check titles include the edition number |
| sessionsource | string | Where the session started, for example `slack`, `teams`, `email`, `report_link`, `latest-link`, `github.com`, `google`, or `(direct)` |
| sessionmedium | string | Session medium. `(not set)` for tagged links, since they carry a source only. Otherwise `(none)` for direct visits, `referral`, or `organic` |
| sessioncampaignname | string | Session campaign. `(not set)` for tagged links, otherwise `(direct)`, `(referral)`, or `(organic)` |
| sessions | bigint | Number of sessions from this source that included this page on this day |
| screenpageviews | bigint | Number of times this page was viewed on this day, in those sessions |
| totalusers | bigint | Number of distinct users in those sessions. Do not sum |
| newusers | bigint | Number of first-time users in those sessions. Do not sum |
| pagepath_redacted | string | `pagepath` with the Signal Check token removed. Derived in the ETL. Filter and group on this |
| page_kind | string | What kind of page this is, one of `signal_check`, `dashboard`, `redirect`, `cookbook`, `preview`, or `other`. Derived in the ETL |

## Notes

**Filter and group on `pagepath_redacted`, never on `pagepath`.** Signal
Check pages are served at a path that includes a private token, so the
links can't be guessed. `pagepath_redacted` drops it.

**Use `page_kind` to pick pages.** It is derived from `pagepath_redacted`,
and the first matching rule wins:

- `signal_check`: a Signal Check edition (`/r/YYYYMMDD_signal-check.html`)
- `redirect`: a redirect page that forwards to the latest edition. These
  are listed by name in the pipeline's ETL job
- `preview`: a Cookbook PR preview (`/canadalogin-metrics-cookbook/pr-preview/`).
  These are the team's own review views, not readership
- `cookbook`: any other Cookbook page
- `dashboard`: any other `.html` page under the publishing site's `/r/`.
  This is a catch-all, so a new dashboard needs no code change. A new
  one-off page there would also count as a dashboard
- `other`: anything else, including `(unrecognized)` paths


**`totalusers` and `newusers` do not sum across rows.** A reader who came
from two sources, or saw two pages, is counted in both rows. This table can't
give an exact count of unique readers of an edition. `sessions` and
`screenpageviews` are safe to sum. The reason is the same as why
[we can't sum unique users](../../cookbook/notes.qmd#daily-unique-users-are-not-the-same-as-period-unique-users)
in IBM Verify.
